subject: Model49 p95 regression — temporary SLA concession requested
messages:
From: PagerDuty Alerts <alerts@pagerduty.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T03:27:12Z
Subject: [Alert] High p95 latency — model49-v2 — eu-west-1

Automatic alert:
- Metric: inference.p95_latency
- Model: model49-v2 (quantized: q8)
- Region: eu-west-1
- Spike: baseline 210ms -> 920ms (03:24 UTC)
- Affected routes: /v1/generate (pin: synthbank-prod)

Immediate info: KV cache TTLs invalidated on a subset of hosts after a staggered rollout of model49-q8 at 03:10. Error rates remain low but tail latency increased on long-context requests (>= 1k tokens).

Attachments: alerts-screenshot-20261101.png, p95-trace-snippet-20261101.txt

Please acknowledge and escalate to on-call SRE if not already assigned.

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T03:42:58Z
Subject: Re: [Alert] High p95 latency — model49-v2 — eu-west-1

Thanks for the notification — I see the same spike in the dashboard. Quick summary of what I think happened: the q8 quant build for model49 had an unexpected KV cache migration path that caused cache misses for batched long-contexts. That surfaces primarily at p95.

Suggested immediate actions (proposal):
1) Roll forward a traffic pin away from model49-q8 to model48-stable for synthbank-prod only (pin at edge routing) — fast to apply, avoids full rollback.
2) Notify the customer and request a short SLA concession window while we remediate (48-72 hours).
3) Mitigate by increasing prefill batching for edge nodes serving synthbank to reduce per-token compute during the window.

Neha — can your team prepare the rollback-pin and a short remediation ETA? Hannah/Marcus — I want a customer comms draft before we contact SynthBank. If we can contain to customer-only routing, we avoid platform-wide SLA variance.

— Vivek

Date: 2026-11-01T04:05:03Z
Subject: Re: Model49 p95 regression — temporary SLA concession requested

Ack'd. SRE can apply an edge-route pin (will be called pin-9847-synthbank) and increase prefill batching for the synthbank route. Timeline:
- Pin deploy: 12 minutes from now (we have a pre-approved edge routing change set).
- Telemetry baseline check: +15m after pin.
- Full rollback (if required): 40 minutes (can revert model variant on dedicated pool).

Root-cause hypothesis: cache key schema change in model49-q8 build; cache miss rate rose to ~28% for long-contexts. We'll push a small hotfix to cache migration logic that should drop misses below 5% in ~24h; full re-quantization and validation will take longer.

I'll pair with Platform QA during the pin so we can confirm p95 recovers before contacting the customer. Attaching short traces.

— Neha

Attachments: p95-trace-snippet-20261101.txt

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Oliver M. <oliver@synthbank.com>, contracts@synthbank.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T04:22:17Z
Subject: Short notice: SynthBank routing change + temporary SLA concession request

Oliver —

I wanted to reach out proactively. Earlier this morning our monitoring flagged a tail-latency increase for requests hitting model49-v2 in eu-west-1 that touches long-context paths used by a subset of your traffic. We are applying a targeted routing pin to move SynthBank production traffic to model48-stable while we validate a remediation for model49-q8. The pin is scoped to SynthBank only and will not impact other customers.

What we need from you: a temporary SLA concession for p95 adherence on the /v1/generate route for the period while we finish remediation. Our ask is: a 72-hour window (starting 2026-11-01T04:25Z) to complete validation and rollback if necessary. We will:
- Keep you updated hourly until the p95 is back within SLA.
- Provide a post-mortem with root cause and mitigation within 5 business days.
- Offer a one-time service credit (pro-rated) should the incident materially exceed the agreed window.

If you agree, please reply to this thread with authorization so we can proceed without delay.

Apologies for the disruption — we're prioritizing SynthBank traffic until this is resolved.

— Marcus Lin
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Marcus — thanks for the quick heads up and the scoped mitigation plan. We appreciate the targeted pin and the willingness to keep SynthBank traffic prioritized.

A couple quick asks from our side before we authorize the concession window:
1) Can you confirm the exact rollback trigger (what metric/time threshold will cause you to revert to model48 permanently for our traffic)?
2) Will there be any change in tokenization/outputs we should expect from model48 compared to model49 that could affect downstream scoring?
3) Please share a single-point-of-contact for hourly updates.

If those three items are confirmed we can authorize a 48-hour concession window starting now, with the option to extend if remediation is progressing.

— Oliver
Head of Platform, SynthBank

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T14:08:45Z
Subject: Final: Approve 48-hour concession + rollback criteria

Following customer approval (Oliver) and SRE telemetry, we are authorizing a 48-hour SLA concession window for SynthBank only (2026-11-01T04:25Z -> 2026-11-03T04:25Z). Conditions and rollback criteria: 

- Rollback (permanent pin to model48-stable) will be triggered if the synthbank p95 remains > 600ms for two consecutive 15-minute windows after the pin has been live for 30 minutes.
- If p95 drops below 400ms for a sustained 30-minute moving window we will begin staged rollback of traffic back to model49-q8 for test traffic only; full de-pinning requires 2 hours of stable telemetry.
- Any client-visible output diffs > 2% on token-level scoring (we will run a side-by-side on a fixed eval set) will halt rollbacks until mitigation or alignment is done.

Actions taken:
- Neha completed the pin and increased prefill batching on 2026-11-01T04:37Z. Telemetry recovered to ~360ms p95 within 20 minutes for the scoped route.
- Marcus notified the customer; Oliver authorized a 48-hour concession.

Next steps:
- Neha and Platform QA to finish the cache migration hotfix validation by 2026-11-03T22:00Z.
- Marcus to send hourly status updates for the duration of the concession window.
- I will sign off on either an extension or full rollback after the validation run and the post-mortem draft.

This thread serves as the authorization record for the concession and rollback criteria.

— Vivek
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
